items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: my first big job with a big band was fantastic. That's the one with a fellow named Gaspard... he asked my folks to let me come and play with them

ctx.x: We had a lot of fun in those days and we enjoyed it. And it would give us a little experience, you know. And then, finally, I began to get better.

And my first big job with a big band was fantastic. That's the one with a fellow named Gaspard and they were looking for a clarinet player. And he used to -- he lived right near my home and he used to hear me every day practicing, so he asked my folks to let me come and play with them on a night job. So they didn't want me to go, anyways, so they -- he begged them, he said he'll take good care of me and bring me home. And one night they had a rehearsal trying to help me get started with the band, and the first…

was 'Tiger Rag.' And when they were finished I was still playing 'Tiger Rag.' That was very embarrassing because I couldn't get that two-four time. You see, I was reading like -- I played from my studies, you know. Four-four was four-four for me and so forth, but it was split time for dance music, you know. And I had a terrible time getting that in my head and especially 'Tiger Rag,' you know. It was so fast and they had all those clarinet breaks in there. Oh, boy. By the time you came to the breaks, they were…
